public_rationale: The main figure is the speaker's own estimate that OpenAI and Anthropic take up 70% or more of Microsoft, Google and Amazon compute capacity. None of those companies discloses capacity allocation by customer, and no credible public estimate was found, so it can be neither confirmed nor refuted. The second part reports his own search and is hedged ('struggled to find'). Public deals such as Jane Street's roughly $6 billion CoreWeave commitment (April 2026) suggest large non-lab buyers exist. But that is a multi-year commitment, not proven annual spend, and it is unclear whether 'them' also excludes hyperscalers. The evidence does not settle the claim.
limitations: Spend figures are contract totals, not annual cash spend.

our_interpretation: The first part is the speaker's estimate of an AI capacity share at the three hyperscalers at about the time of the post (mid-2026). It would be checkable only with disclosed or credibly reported capacity allocations.

The second part reports his own search. The testable core is whether, at the time of the post, neocloud customers other than OpenAI and Anthropic were publicly known to spend more than $50 million a year. 'Them' may also cover the hyperscalers, because the same post lists Microsoft and NVIDIA as large CoreWeave customers.
Target period: the first seven months of 2026 up to the post, as the most recent state public evidence could describe.
criteria.support_condition: Credible data show OpenAI and Anthropic using at least 70% of the three hyperscalers' (AI) compute capacity, and no other customer of non-hyperscale providers publicly known to spend over $50 million a year.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible data show OpenAI and Anthropic using well under 70% of that capacity, or several non-OpenAI, non-Anthropic, non-hyperscaler customers of neoclouds clearly spending over $50 million a year.
